topics.topic: Whether scratch-space limits apply continuously during execution or only to final retained files
questions: Which passage must change: must scratch use remain bounded throughout execution, or may code exceed the total ceiling transiently and evade the bound by removing files before the end?

quotes: one fresh private exchange directory bound read-write whose use is bounded by the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant twice — each file written in it by the runner's setrlimit file-size limit, and the scratch total by the parent, measured once when the environment has ended — the st_size of each distinct regular file (by inode) under the exchange directory, the files the parent put there excluded, directories and symbolic links counting nothing and a file removed before the end not counted — a total above that constant being a resource hit —, bubblewrap's own fresh proc and minimal dev mounts, and no other host directory;
judgement.why: The text specifies a continuous per-file limit and a total scratch limit measured only after execution, explicitly excluding files removed before the final measurement.
